div.div: The smallest is always on top, so the heap evicts exactly the item least likely to belong in the answer. Whatever survives is the top K.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 340px; height: 1px; padding-top: 271px; margin-left: 438px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-ok-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-ok-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Sorting the whole stream is O(N log N) and throws away most of the work. Bounding the heap at K keeps each insert at log K.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 758px; height: 1px; padding-top: 357px; margin-left: 38px;

div.div: Reach for a heap when you need the extreme repeatedly, not the whole order. Sorting answers a question you were not asked.
